subject: Re: MAP alignment & commit cadence — proposed ramp and pricing triggers
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@scaleapps.com>
Cc: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@scaleapps.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + initial commit cadence questions

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps evaluation milestones to commercial checkpoints. High level asks:

- Confirm that TPM (tokens per month) is the right consumption unit for your internal forecasting.
- Agree on a pragmatic ramp schedule we can tie to discounts and guaranteed capacity.
- Identify any legal/procurement milestones you need before we route the DocuSign.

Key proposal (summary):
- 60-day eval window with a 60k TPM cap for month 1, 300k TPM for month 2, then transition into a committed cadence.
- Commit tiers: 500k TPM monthly commit initial (month 3–6), scale to 1.25M TPM by month 9.
- Pricing: list price for dev/eval months, then 12% discount once committed to 500k TPM, an additional 8% (20% total) after sustained 1.25M TPM for 2 consecutive months.
- SLA/priority: Dedicated capacity during business hours after commit; fallback to hosted during off hours.

I attached the MAP PDF and a simple pricing_schedule.xlsx so you can run numbers. I left placeholders for procurement lead and DocuSign timeline. If TPM isn't your forecasting unit, tell me what you prefer and I’ll convert.

Would love to lock on this by next Friday so legal can start redlines. Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Thursday to walk through the MAP and lock the month-by-month targets.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_ScaleApps_Redwood_v1.pdf (application/pdf), pricing_schedule.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@scaleapps.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@scaleapps.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + initial commit cadence questions

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clean MAP. A couple of clarifying items from our side before we commit to the sync:

1) TPM unit: yes, we measure monthly token consumption (TPM) in our finance forecasts.
2) Ramp profile: month 1/2 look fine, but our internal ops team expects a slower ramp to committed capacity. We're more comfortable with a 400k TPM initial commit (month 3–5) then stepping to 900k TPM by month 8, with the same discount structure you proposed.
3) Discount triggers: can you make the 12% initial discount retroactive for the entire billing month in which the commit is signed, not from the following invoice?
4) Evaluation SLA: during the eval we need predictable latency under 200ms 95th pct for short responses — can you confirm if the hosted tier meets that or whether we should include a short Dedicated trial?

Also, procurement wants to see a single-sheet commercial summary (we'll circulate internally). Could you add a one-line summary per milestone (what we get, what we pay, who signs)?

We can do the Thursday sync — propose 10:00am PT.

Thanks,

Maria Alvarez
VP Product
ScaleApps
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MAP draft + initial commit cadence questions (notes & counterproposal)

Soojin / Grace —

Looping in a quick internal note ahead of the 10:00am PT sync with ScaleApps. Short answers and a suggested counter to Maria's slower ramp ask:

- Retroactive discount: Legal's usual stance is discount from signing date forward (not retroactive). We can make an exception as a one-time credit on the first invoice to approximate retroactivity. Recommend offering that as a concession.

- Ramp compromise: propose the following blended path to get them comfortable while preserving economics:
  * Eval months: M1=60k TPM (no commit), M2=240k TPM (no commit).
  * Initial commit (signed at start of M3): 450k TPM monthly for M3–M5 with a 10% introductory discount (instead of 12%) and a one-time invoice credit equal to the difference should they hit 500k TPM for any of M3–M5. This reduces our near-term exposure while giving them the upside to hit the 500k trigger.
  * Scale trigger: when sustained 1.0M TPM for 2 months, upgrade discount to 20% and guarantee dedicated capacity during business hours.

- SLA: We can commit that hosted will meet <200ms 95th for short responses for their pilot traffic patterns; if they need stricter guarantees we'll propose a short 30-day Dedicated trial run (we cover the setup).

- Procurement one-pager: I've drafted a short commercial summary (I will paste below in the meeting).

If you both are okay, we'll present this blended counter. It preserves our margin, gives them runway to ramp, and keeps the scaling incentives in place.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Director, Sales
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0124

--- pasted commercial summary (for meeting) ---
1) Eval (M1–M2): free credits + standard hosted rates; objective: feature/latency validation (60k -> 240k TPM).
2) Initial commit (M3–M5): 450k TPM monthly commit, 10% discount, one-time credit if 500k TPM is reached in M3–M5.
3) Scale (M6+): sustained 1.0M TPM for 2 months -> escalate to 20% discount and dedicated-hours capacity; option to renegotiate SLA/throughput for peak windows.

Attachments referenced for meeting: MAP_ScaleApps_Redwood_v1.pdf, pricing_schedule.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@scaleapps.com>
Cc: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@scaleapps.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + initial commit cadence questions — agreed next steps

Hi Maria / Ana —

Thanks for the questions and for confirming TPM as your forecast unit. Per our internal alignment (Ben / Grace), here's a concise, agreed-upon MAP variant we can present in the procurement one-pager and that we'll attach to the DocuSign:

Summary (agreed variant):
- Eval (M1–M2): 60k TPM (M1), 240k TPM (M2). Hosted access, standard eval credits. Goal: latency validation (<200ms 95th for short responses) and integration checklist completion.
- Commit (M3–M5): Signed commit at 450k TPM monthly. 10% committed discount applied from signing date. If actual consumption >= 500k TPM in any of M3–M5, Redwood will apply a one-time invoice credit equal to the pricing delta to make the effective discount equal to 12% for that month.
- Scale (M6+): If ScaleApps sustains >= 1.0M TPM for two consecutive months, discount upgrades to 20% and Redwood will provide Dedicated-hours capacity (09:00–18:00 PT) plus a throughput review to adjust autoscaling policies.

Additional commercial notes:
- Retroactive vs credit: we agreed to the invoice credit approach to approximate retroactivity while keeping contract language simple.
- SLA: Hosted tier meets the latency target based on pilot profile; we'll sponsor a 30-day Dedicated trial if you want deterministic isolation during the eval.
- Procurement one-pager: attached (single-sheet commercial summary).

Next steps:
1) Thursday 10:00am PT — 30-min sync to walk the one-pager and confirm signatories. (Calendar invite sent.)
2) Procurement provides preferred PO/legal reviewer by EOD Fri 9/3.
3) Redwood will prepare DocuSign with the agreed MAP and pricing sheet immediately after the sync.

I've attached the MAP PDF and the updated pricing_schedule.xlsx (reflected the 450k/1.0M triggers and the invoice credit language). DocuSign link will follow in the post-meeting email.

Thanks — looking forward to getting ScaleApps set up.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
